gen-gf-oxanium-gf-noto-sans-telugu: Commanding and a little sharp, Oxanium draws big lowercase with open curve ends. Noto Sans Telugu sits beneath it, its counters connected to the outside and its midline set high.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-noto-sans-thai: Noto Sans Thai reads soft and friendly, like inflated beads. Underneath Oxanium's flat, unmodulated lines, its rounded letters stay open, so a long passage would feel easygoing and unhurried.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-noto-sans-warang-citi: Oxanium leads with a monoline build and tall, confident lowercase. Noto Sans Warang Citi follows in a plain sans, its words forming solid blocks, so a long passage feels tidy and steady.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-noto-sans-yi: Modern and businesslike, this pairing starts with Noto Sans Yi's deep midsection. Its strongest quality is the push and pull between that body and Oxanium, whose letter parts carry matching visual mass.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-noto-sans-zanabazar-sq: Big lowercase, no hairlines, and a body that soars just as high on the line. Oxanium's solid strokes hold the top while Noto Sans Zanabazar Square keeps tiny sizes crisp.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-noto-traditional-nushu: Oxanium's joins never thin where strokes meet, which gives its headings real weight. Yet Noto Traditional Nushu is the one that feels human, with broad-nibbed strokes and bowls that fill the line.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-numans: Clean and modern, Numans spreads its tightly coiled lowercase across wide tracking, with an s whose ends hang far from the spine. Oxanium holds it steady.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-onest: Oxanium's monoline strokes and tall lowercase give it a sharp, commanding look. Onest settles underneath with short ascenders above big bowls, a gentle line that never pools ink.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-orienta: Orienta feels modern and breathy. Oxanium handles the heading with curves showing no stress at all, while Orienta, a plain sans, keeps its counters open and its capitals close to the lowercase in height.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-oxygen: Oxygen keeps its curves open and its lowercase close to capital height. Oxygen is a sans-serif that reads cleanly across many lines, while Oxanium's horizontals match its verticals in thickness above it.
